job.name: Job
job.note: The afflicted just man of Hus, defending his innocence before his friends and God.

1.t: I made a covenant with my eyes, that I would not so much as think upon a virgin.

2.t: For what part should God from above have in me, and what inheritance the Almighty from on high?

3.t: Is not destruction to the wicked, and aversion to them that work iniquity?

4.t: Doth not he consider my ways, and number all my steps?

5.t: If I have walked in vanity, and my foot hath made haste to deceit:

6.t: Let him weigh me in a just balance, and let God know my simplicity.

7.t: If my step hath turned out of the way, and if my heart hath followed my eyes, and if a spot hath cleaved to my hands:

8.t: Then let me sow and let another reap: and let my offspring be rooted out.

9.t: If my heart hath been deceived upon a woman, and if I have laid wait at my friend's door:

10.t: Let my wife be the harlot of another, and let other men lie with her.

11.t: For this is a heinous crime, and a most grievous iniquity.

12.t: It is a fire that devoureth even to destruction, and rooteth up all things that spring.

13.t: If I have despised to abide judgment with my manservant, or my maidservant, when they had any controversy against me:

14.t: For what shall I do when God shall rise to judge? and when he shall examine, what shall I answer him?

15.t: Did not he that made me in the womb make him also: and did not one and the same form me in the womb?

16.t: If I have denied to the poor what they desired, and have made the eyes of the widow wait:

17.t: If I have eaten my morsel alone, and the fatherless hath not eaten thereof:

18.t: (For from my infancy mercy grew up with me: and it came out with me from my mother's womb:)

19.t: If I have despised him that was perishing for want of clothing, and the poor man that had no covering:

20.t: If his sides have not blessed me, and if he were not warmed with the fleece of my sheep:

21.t: If I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, even when I saw myself superior in the gate:

22.t: Let my shoulder fall from its joint, and let my arm with its bones be broken.

23.t: For I have always feared God as waves swelling over me, and his weight I was unable to bear.

24.t: If I have thought gold my strength, and have said to fine gold: My confidence:

25.t: If I have rejoiced over my great riches, and because my hand had gotten much.

26.t: If I beheld the sun when it shined and the moon going in brightness:

27.t: And my heart in secret hath rejoiced, and I have kissed my hand with my mouth:

28.t: Which is a very great iniquity, and a denial against the most high God.

29.t: If I have been glad at the downfall of him that hated me, and have rejoiced that evil had found him.

30.t: For I have not given my mouth to sin, by wishing a curse to his soul.

31.t: If the men of my tabernacle have not said: Who will give us of his flesh that we may be filled?

32.t: The stranger did not stay without, my door was open to the traveller.

33.t: If as a man I have hid my sin, and have concealed my iniquity in my bosom.

34.t: If I have been afraid at a very great multitude, and the contempt of kinsmen hath terrified me: and have not rather held my peace, and not gone out of the door.

35.t: Who would grant me a hearing, that the Almighty may hear my desire: and that he himself that judgeth would write a book,

36.t: That I may carry it on my shoulder, and put it about me as a crown?

37.t: At every step of mine I would pronounce it, and offer it as to a prince.

38.t: If my land cry against me, and with it the furrows thereof mourn:

39.t: If I have eaten the fruits thereof without money, and have afflicted the son of the tillers thereof:

40.t: Let thistles grow up to me instead of wheat, and thorns instead of barley.
